specFirst: Written BEFORE the code, per skills/agentsBestPractices.md §1. This file, spec.md and README.md are the design record. Approved by the product owner on 2026-09-02 (session plan: binary-purring-lobster). AMENDED TWICE on 2026-09-08, both in session with the product owner: v2 for the page defs format change (prose definition, pipeline-only write), and v3 after MEASURING v2 on a real page — the shared defs is read for the region analysis, the target stays the file passed in the argument, and nothing in the shared is ever written.
description: Given an explicit catalogProject and the reference of an existing page .defs.ts, decides which molecule (group + tag) serves each region of that page and rewrites ONLY that file's `pipeline` — the chosen molecules' source files appended to pipeline[0].dependsFiles and their groups' usage contracts to pipeline[0].skills. The regions are extracted DETERMINISTICALLY from the workspace shared defs (read-only) and the page's own prose `definition` supplies the page intent; neither is ever written. Writes nothing else: no report, no l4 artifact, no trace file. A sibling of agentChooseMolecules (the probe that only measures), built to actually equip a page.
principles: ZERO ARTIFACT RULE. The only file this agent ever writes is the target .defs.ts, and inside it only the `pipeline` value (steps/c3-patch). Every handoff between steps travels through the task tree's own step `result` field (helpers/cm2Types.cm2ReadC1Result / cm2ReadGroupResult) — never a file. No report.json, no c1-groups.json, no per-attempt trace, no l4 folder anywhere, in any project.

THE TARGET IS THE ARGUMENT, AND EVERY OTHER FILE IS READ-ONLY. The run reads the workspace shared defs, the contract it declares, the catalog and the target's own prose; it writes the target's `pipeline` and nothing else. The shared is analysis, never a destination — no run may amend the workspace to make a page equippable.

THE DEFINITION IS READ-ONLY TOO. `export const definition` is prose and is spliced back byte for byte: the only cut this agent makes is around the `pipeline` value, so a run can never change what the page says it is.

EXPLICIT CATALOG, NO DISCOVERY. catalogProject arrives in the mention argument. There is no dependency search, no chChooseCatalog, no 'more than one catalog reachable' ambiguity — all of that existed in the probe only because it never received the project.

REGIONS ARE DETERMINISTIC, NEVER INVENTED. helpers/cm2Regions.extractRegions walks the workspace's own dataBindings[]/inputs[]. No LLM ever decides what counts as a region — c1-groups only decides which GROUP covers a region already handed to it, and its answer is checked against the list that was sent (steps/c1-groups.checkRegionSet).

THE CATALOG IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF TAGS. Same anti-invention gate as agentChooseMolecules, imported unchanged from its steps/c1-groups/gate.ts and steps/c2-molecules/gate.ts — a tag outside the group's published list is refused by a deterministic gate, never completed by code.
ONE CATALOG LEVEL PER PROMPT. c1 sees level 1 (the group list); each c2 sees level 2 of ONE group. Same funnel and the same reason as the probe: the whole catalog does not fit a prompt.

PERSISTED SHAPE IS MINIMAL, AND IT IS THE PIPELINE. Two flat arrays of file references — no reason, no scenarioUsed, no region name, no gate history. What reaches the render model is what materialize reads: dependsFiles as context sections, skills concatenated into its system prompt.

decisions.argument: The whole mention is one JSON object, '{"catalogProject": N, "target": "..."}', parsed with plain JSON.parse (helpers/cm2Entry.cm2ParseEntry) — the same choice agentChangeFrontend's 'only-materialize' command already made for a single flat-object argument. Both keys required; no free prose, no optional-prefix-plus-prose shape (unlike agentChooseMolecules's chParseEntry), so there is no reason to reach for mls.common.safeParseArgs or hand-rolled brace-matching.
decisions.bootstrap: Deterministic (skipRootLLM: true on the initial add-message-ai), same gesture as agentChangeFrontend.ts's beforePromptImplicit. There is no c0-classify: nothing here needs classifying, and the run does not want to spend a call on it.
decisions.regionGranularity: FOUR kinds. (1) surface: one per query dataBinding — the list/table/selector of its rows, at `binding.id`. (2) entry: one per 'form' input, at `binding.id::inputName` — on a COMMAND it is a field of the record being written, on a QUERY it is a FILTER or SORT control of the listing, and the need line says which, because a search box and a text field are not the same choice. (3) trigger: one per COMMAND dataBinding, at `binding.id` (a binding is a query or a command, never both). (4) page: a need serving the whole page, at `page::<role>` — today only `page::feedback`, emitted when the page has at least one command. 'selection'/'route' inputs are never regions (populated by picking a row elsewhere, or by the URL), but their COUNT is stated in the surface's need, because a list whose rows feed a command's selected id is a selector rather than a passive table. ⚠️ A QUERY'S OWN form inputs became regions in v3, caught by cm2Regions' own test: v1 extracted entries from command inputs only, so ticketCatalogue's `search`/`sortBy`/`sortOrder` produced nothing at all. A typed input is a typed input whichever kind of binding declares it.
decisions.patchTarget: The SAME file passed in target — page11, page12 or any future genome sharing the { definition, pipeline } shape. This agent does not decide which genome gets molecules; whoever calls it decides which file to point at.
decisions.modelType: reasoning + x-tool-strict on both LLM steps (c1-groups, c2-molecules), per skills/modelTypes.md and the agentChooseMolecules precedent. No classifier model anywhere.
decisions.retry: One retry with the gate errors in the prompt (CM2_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2), same budget as the probe. A c2 that still fails after 2 attempts records ok:false and completes — c3-patch leaves that group's regions untouched rather than failing the whole run. FIXED 2026-09-08: the c2 retry step used to be planted without `target`, so the second attempt lost both the page context and the project language — the tie-breakers the first attempt had. The retry prompt now carries target, like c1's always did.
decisions.idempotency: c3-patch compares the rewritten source to the original before writing; a rerun that changes nothing touches no file at all. A region already annotated is reconciled (overwritten or removed), never duplicated.
decisions.projectContext: 2026-09 addendum, measured on _102046_/approveChangeOrder: c2 (not c1 — group choice does not need locale) also reads the TARGET project's own l5/project.json (helpers/cm2ProjectContext.ts) for its declared language(s), added as a 'Project context' prompt section. This is what lets c2 pick between locale-bound siblings (e.g. groupEnterMoney's en-US vs pt-BR molecules) instead of correctly-but-avoidably answering 'none' for lack of any signal. Still a DECLARED fact, never an inference — same category as the contract's own field types, just sourced from l5. Absent/unreadable l5/project.json -> the section is omitted, never padded with a default.
decisions.pageContextC1: v2 (2026-09-08): c1 receives the whole prose `definition` as its human prompt, so there is no separate {{pageContext}} block for it any more — the prose IS the page context. c2, which never sees the definition, still gets it as a section: helpers/cm2PageContext now parses the four labelled prose lines instead of purpose/presentation.categoryRef/pageObjective, and `uxExperience` (processWizard, entityRecordManagement, dashboardCommandCenter, ...) is the declared experience shape that took over from presentation.categoryRef in the c2 prompt's 'the catch-all row is the trap' step. 2026-09-04, SUPERSEDES the 'c1 was left alone' decision below: c1 now gets {{pageContext}} too. The earlier reasoning was that c1 had no measured defect — but comparing against the probe on clientCatalogue/page21 showed it does: c1 sent the client list to groupViewTable while the probe sent it to groupSelectOne (ml-listbox-sidebar-select), and the target's own pageObjective declares 'master-detail list with contextual selection' plus the anti-pattern 'Usar um seletor livre de identificadores para editar ou excluir'. A list whose rows feed a command's selected id is a SELECTOR, and groupSelectOne is where the selector siblings live (it even publishes ml-table-single-select). c1 was not correct, it was correct-looking in isolation.
decisions.pageContext: 2026-09-04 addendum, from a measured instability: across two runs of the SAME page, c1 chose the right group every time and c2 flip-flopped inside it — ml-data-table vs ml-view-table (11 siblings), ml-multiline-text vs ml-enter-text (8), ml-radio-group vs nothing (12) — while groupEnterMoney (2 siblings) stayed stable. Instability scaling with sibling count is the signature of missing discriminating evidence, and the catalog was NOT the gap: groupViewTable's skill text ships 10 scenario rows, 11 full descriptions and their layout axes. The gap was the mechanical `need` line, which matched only the catch-all scenario row ('Listagem geral com ordenação e paginação' — which recommends 10 of 11). FIX: c2 now also reads the target page's own declared intent (helpers/cm2PageContext.ts) — purpose, presentation.categoryRef and, on the goal-first genomes, the whole pageObjective (jobToBeDone, primaryDecision, usageFrequency, decisiveInfo, informationHierarchy, antiPatterns, criticalActions[].presentation) — plus one structural fact counted from the defs: how many command inputs are fed by a row selection. ~2.3KB on the measured page, against a 2-6KB group catalog. Read FRESH from the target in c2 rather than threaded through c1's result (which every later step reads). c1 was deliberately LEFT ALONE: it was already 100% correct on both runs, and changing a step with no measured defect is how a fix becomes a regression (agentsBestPractices: 'structural refactors ship with identical external behavior'). page11 has no pageObjective, so there the section degrades to purpose+categoryRef; a defs declaring none of it gets no section at all.
decisions.needLine: 2026-09-04: cm2Regions also states, per entry region, the input's declared `required` flag and HOW MANY typed (presentation:'form') fields the same command has — a one-field command is a single decision, a five-field one is a form, and that changes which sibling fits. Both are facts the defs already carries and this agent was discarding. Still nothing inferred from a field name.
decisions.referenceForm: 2026-09-04, measured then corrected: TWO reference forms exist and are not interchangeable. IMPORT form ('/_102020_/.../usage' — leading slash, no extension) is what `await import()` takes and what a group's index.defs.ts publishes in `usageContract`. PIPELINE form ('_102020_/.../usage.ts' — no leading slash, with extension) is what pipeline[].skills/dependsFiles take. This agent was writing the import form into the pipeline, and agentCfeMaterializeGen SILENTLY dropped every such entry (readSections/readContextSections skip an empty read), so a usage contract that never reached the model was indistinguishable from one never listed: 4 of 6 skills and 6 of 8 dependsFiles were lost. Every reference this agent puts in a pipeline array now goes through cm2Types.cm2PipelineRef. Target form settled by the platform's own generator, not by inference: across every .defs.ts agentChangeFrontend wrote in a real client project, no pipeline reference carries a leading slash. Consequence for the render skill (genCfePage21RenderTs): the runtime import is now built from the dependsFiles entry by prepending '/' and swapping '.ts' for '.js', not by appending '.js'.
decisions.definitionFormat: 2026-09-08 — THE FORMAT CHANGED, AND THAT IS WHAT STARTED v2. A page .defs.ts used to carry `export const definition = { pageId, purpose, presentation, pageObjective, dataBindings[] }` (mls-102046). It now carries a TEMPLATE LITERAL of prose (all three genomes of _102047_): four labelled lines — `page:`, `actor:`, `purpose:`, `uxExperience:` — plus a fixed closing paragraph addressed to the render model. The structural facts did not vanish, they MOVED to the workspace shared defs, which is where v3 reads them from (see decisions.regionSource). A target still carrying the v1 object definition is refused with an error naming that shape, never parsed on a guess.
decisions.whatIsWritten: 2026-09-08 — THE PIPELINE, AND NOTHING ELSE. With a prose definition there is no dataBinding or input node left to carry `molecule: { group, tag }`, so the whole annotation path (applyMoleculeChoices, the root pageMolecules[] array and its role vocabulary) is retired with the object it addressed. Nor is a new pipeline KEY an option: PipelineItem (cfeMaterializeCore.ts) is a closed interface and materialize reads exactly two of its fields, so an extra key would be dropped in silence. So the output is the two arrays that do reach the render model: dependsFiles gets the chosen molecules' own .ts files (read back as '## Context files' sections) and skills gets their groups' usage contracts (concatenated into the render system prompt). The region→molecule MAPPING is therefore not persisted; genCfePage21RenderTs.ts's '## Molecules' section was rewritten on the same day to place each chosen molecule itself.
decisions.pipelineReconciliation: 2026-09-08 — the pipeline is now the ONLY output, so appending to it is not enough: a rerun whose choice CHANGED would leave the previous molecule in dependsFiles forever and the render model would get two components for one region. c3-patch therefore PRUNES this agent's own entries before adding the current ones, recognized by shape and by shape only — dependsFiles matching l2/molecules/<group>/<name>.ts, skills matching l2/aura/molecules/skills/<group>/usage.ts. Everything the generator put there (web/shared/<page>Dts.txt, designSystem.ts, genCfePage21RenderTs.ts, the collabux template) matches neither pattern and survives untouched. Added entries are SORTED, so a rerun that chose the same set writes nothing even when c1 happened to return the groups in another order — without that, the byte-equality idempotency check would fire on ordering alone.
decisions.pageMoleculeShape_retired_v2: RETIRED 2026-09-08 by decisions.definitionFormat / whatIsWritten. Kept as the record of what v1 did: 2026-09-04: a region serving the WHOLE page has no binding node to carry `molecule`, so it lands in a ROOT array — `pageMolecules: [{ role, group, tag }]` — addressed by the region id `page::<role>` (unambiguous: every binding id this platform generates starts with `binding.`). ARRAY WITH A ROLE, not one field per role (`moleculeFeedback`, `moleculeConfirmation`, ...), because destructive-confirmation and workflow-progress are already known roles and a vocabulary grows without changing the shape; the vocabulary is CLOSED and extended deliberately, holding `feedback` only today. ROOT, not nested under `presentation` (where categoryRef lives): `presentation` is agentChangeFrontend's object, and this agent's output inside it would be exposed to a partial rewrite by its owner — at the root, pageMolecules is unambiguously this agent's, the same clarity of ownership `molecule` has inside a binding, which had no alternative. Safe typewise: `definition` carries no `satisfies` (unlike `pipeline`, which is `as const`). Reconciliation is per role — a rerun replaces its own role and keeps the others; answering none for the last role deletes the key rather than leaving `pageMolecules: []`.
decisions.triggerRegion_retired_v2: RETIRED 2026-09-08 by decisions.definitionFormat / whatIsWritten. Kept as the record of what v1 did: 2026-09-04, measured by running the probe and this agent on the SAME file (_102046_ clientCatalogue/page21): the probe found 12 regions to this agent's 7, and 3 of the 5 it could not see were the buttons executing cmdCreateClient/cmdUpdateClient/cmdDeleteClient — which the probe routed to groupTriggerAction, an entire group unreachable from here. Sharpest case: cmdDeleteClient has NO 'form' input (its only input is the selected id), so the whole command binding produced zero regions and vanished from the answer. A command's own trigger is as much a molecule-serving interaction as any field, and it is fully derivable — every command binding has exactly one. After the fix the same file yields 10 regions, covering 10 of the probe's 12.
decisions.typeResolution_retired_v2: RETIRED 2026-09-08 by decisions.definitionFormat / whatIsWritten. Kept as the record of what v1 did: Field types come from the sibling web/contracts/{page} file: its .defs.ts first (source of truth), a regex fallback over its compiled .ts when the .defs.ts is not on disk (confirmed necessary on a real client project, mls-102046, where only the .ts was present locally). An unresolved type is honestly 'unknown', never guessed from the field name — same rule the catalog's own usage guidance already states.
decisions.regionSource: v3, 2026-09-08 — MEASURED, then changed. v2 read only the target's prose definition and produced ONE region for _102047_ page21/ticketCatalogue, so one molecule (groupviewtable--ml-lcrud-detail-grid) was chosen for a screen that also has 7 typed command fields, 3 typed listing filters, 4 command triggers, 3 listing surfaces and 4 declared success/error messages. NOT the model's fault and NOT the catalog's: every group needed is published (groupEnterText 8, groupSelectOne 12, groupTriggerAction 6, groupNotifyUser 4, groupSearchContent 4). The cause was the SOURCE: `page11DefinitionProse` (agentChangeFrontend/helpers/cfeCreateShared.ts) is a fixed four-line template — pageName, actor, purpose, categoryRef — plus one boilerplate paragraph, and `defsFormat: 'prose'` is hardcoded for every genome and every category (cfePageRecipe.ts, with a test asserting it), so the prose can never name a field, a command or a control on ANY page. Sharpest evidence that the choice was coherent all along: the molecule c2 picked declares in its own defs that the record detail content 'is supplied by the consumer' inside its `Detail` content area — the container names the hole the missing molecules belong in. SO: regions now come from `web/shared/{page}.defs.ts` (helpers/cm2Shared, READ-ONLY), which still publishes dataBindings[] in the same shape v1 walked, and which is where the platform's own gates read them from (cfeMaterializeCore.pageDefinitionForChecks: 'page11: the workspace shared map... the prose definition has neither'). The generator says the same thing in pageLayoutDefsExport's own comment: 'the structured map lives once on the workspace shared defs; gates read it from there'. Same page after the change: 18 regions.
decisions.twoSourcesOneWrite: v3 — the run reads TWO files for analysis and writes ONE, and they answer different questions. The SHARED says WHAT INTERACTIONS EXIST (dataBindings, the declared column/field labels, destructiveCommandIds, contractRef.tsPath). The TARGET's prose says WHAT THE PAGE IS FOR (uxExperience, purpose, actor — helpers/cm2PageContext), which is the c2 evidence that rules a specific scenario row in or out. The target passed in the argument stays the only file written, and only its `pipeline` value: the shared is never amended, not even to add something that would make a page easier to equip. Reverse derivation is deliberately absent — the shared's own `layoutRef.defPath` names ONE genome (page11), so it could never say which target a run was pointed at.
decisions.contractPathIsDeclared: v3 — field types come from the contract the SHARED declares in `contractRef.tsPath`, not from the `web/contracts/{page}` convention v1 had to re-derive. Its `.defs.ts` is preferred when present (source of truth) and the materialized `.ts` is the fallback — in practice the only one on disk, confirmed on both mls-102046 and mls-102047, whose `web/contracts/` holds `.ts` files only. An unresolved type is honestly 'unknown' in the need line, never guessed from the field name. Worth recording: on ticketCatalogue this resolved `status` to the literal union `'open' | 'closed'`, which is exactly what makes a select choosable over a text field — the known platform gap (a status degrading to plain `string`) did not occur.
decisions.declaredLabelsAsEvidence: v3 — the need lines carry the workspace's DECLARED i18n labels: 'intent.<cmd>.list.column.<field>.label' for a surface's columns, 'intent.<cmd>.form.field.<name>.label' for a command field, 'intent.<cmd>.list.filter.<name>.label' for a listing control. This is the discriminating evidence v1 never had: a surface need line that said only 'Listar Chamado — returns fields: ...' matched every group's catch-all scenario row, which is what made c2 flip-flop between 11 near-siblings across two runs of the same page. Declared facts, in the module's own language — never inferred.
decisions.destructiveIsDeclared: v3 — a command listed in the shared's `destructiveCommandIds` has that stated in its trigger's need line. v1's knownGaps said a destructive confirmation 'cannot be tied to a specific binding deterministically, since knowing cmdDeleteClient is destructive means reading its NAME'. That stopped being true when the structure moved: the shared publishes the list. The trigger is judged as destructive; the blocking CONFIRMATION dialog remains a gap because no published group covers one, which is the probe's own honest null.
decisions.regionSetGate: v3 — c1's answer is checked against the region list that was actually sent (steps/c1-groups.checkRegionSet): a renamed region cannot be joined to anything and a dropped one loses its molecule in silence, with the run still reporting success. The imported gate CANNOT do this — runChGroupsGate comes from the probe, where regions are invented by the model and there is no list to check against, so it only refuses an empty answer, a nameless region, a duplicate and an unpublished group. The c2 gate already checked its own region set (region_unknown / region_unanswered); this closes the same hole one level up, and it is only checkable BECAUSE the regions are deterministic.

conventions.target: An import-style reference to a page .defs.ts, e.g. '_102046_/l2/buildFlowFsm/web/desktop/page11/approveChangeOrder.defs' — decoded by agentChooseMolecules's chFileRefFromImport (reused, not duplicated). Must resolve to extension '.defs.ts'.
conventions.contractPath: Declared by the shared as `contractRef.tsPath` — no convention to re-derive (v1 guessed `web/contracts/{page}`). READ-ONLY, and best-effort: an unresolvable type is 'unknown' in the need line.
conventions.handoff: c1's result carries { catalogProject, target, regions, groups } forward; each c2's result carries { group, ok, choices, usageContract }. Both are read back via getAllSteps + planId match on the done-anchor (helpers/cm2Types.cm2ReadStepResult) — the exact mechanism agentChooseMolecules's own fan-out already uses to read c1, generalized to every subsequent read in this agent.
conventions.writesNothingElse: No molecule, no usage contract, no group index, no todoFrontend/statusFrontend change, no config.json, no materialization — and, inside the target itself, nothing but the `pipeline` value. Turning the equipped pipeline into rendered markup is agentCfeMaterializeGen's job, out of scope here.
conventions.definitionRead: The prose of `export const definition` of the TARGET, read verbatim between its backticks (helpers/cm2DefsPatch.parsePageDefsSource) and used for the page intent only. A file whose definition is still the v1 JSON OBJECT is refused with an error that says so by name.
conventions.sharedPath: Derived from the target: same project/level, folder truncated at and including its 'web' segment plus 'shared', same shortName (helpers/cm2Shared.cm2SharedFileFromTarget). Generic across page11/page21/page31 and any future device/layout naming. READ-ONLY. A target with no 'web' segment, or one that already points at the shared, fails with a readable error instead of guessing.

treeOverview: c1-groups            deterministic regions (shared defs, read-only) + the target's prose intent + level 1 -> the group of each, or none
c1r-fanout            the root again: plants one c2 per chosen group, plus c3-patch
c2-<group>          level 2 of that group -> LLM decides molecule per region (anti-invention gate)
c3-patch              deterministic: rewrites the target's pipeline — the run's only write

steps.goal: Extract regions deterministically from the target's dataBindings/inputs (+ sibling contract types) and ask the LLM which published group covers each, or none.

gate.onFail: retry 1 with errors in the prompt; a 2nd failure fails the step

steps.result: { catalogProject, target, regions: ChRegion[], groups: string[] } — read back by c1r-fanout and c3-patch, never written to disk

steps.goal: Read c1's result from the task tree and plant one c2 per DISTINCT group, plus c3-patch depending on all of them. With no group chosen, c3-patch still runs alone.
For ONE group: choose the molecule for each region c1 assigned to it. Never fails the run — a gate that refuses twice records ok:false and completes anyway.

gate.onFail: retry 1 with errors in the prompt; a 2nd failure records ok:false and completes

steps.result: { group, ok, choices: [{region, tag}], usageContract } — never written to disk

steps.goal: Join c1's regions with every c2 group's accepted choices, patch definition + pipeline, and rewrite the target .defs.ts. Skips the write entirely when nothing changed.

artifacts.the target .defs.ts (its `pipeline` valu: the ONLY file this agent writes. `export const definition` is not part of the cut and the workspace shared defs is never written at all: pipeline[0].dependsFiles gets the chosen molecules' own .ts files and pipeline[0].skills their groups' usage contracts, this agent's own previous entries pruned first and the new ones sorted (decisions.pipelineReconciliation)

outOfScope: a molecule-aware render skill that composes markup from the equipped pipeline — this agent only equips it (genCfePage21RenderTs.ts's '## Molecules' section is that consumer)
WRITING anything to the workspace shared defs, the contract, or any file other than the target's pipeline — the shared is analysis only
annotating the v1 JSON-object definition (`molecule: {group, tag}` on a binding, the root pageMolecules[] array) — retired with the format
creating the target file — the caller decides which file to point this agent at
catalog dependency discovery — the caller must know which project's catalog answers, and pass it explicitly

knownGaps.mappingNotPersisted: the region→molecule decision is not written anywhere (decisions.whatIsWritten): the pipeline carries the chosen components as a flat set, so the render model decides which one serves which region (genCfePage21RenderTs.ts's '## Molecules'). Nothing downstream can audit the choice from the file alone.
knownGaps.destructiveConfirmation: no published group covers a BLOCKING confirmation dialog, and the probe itself honestly answered null for it. What v3 did fix is the input: `destructiveCommandIds` is declared by the shared, so the destructive command's TRIGGER is judged as destructive. If a confirmation group ever ships, its address is `page::confirmation` and it needs no new shape.
knownGaps.scenariesUnused: the shared also publishes `scenaries[]` (base / detail / one per command, with their preconditions) and this agent does not read it. It is the declared scene structure of the page and it would sharpen the record-detail axis — the one that separates a lcrud-detail-grid from a plain table. Left out deliberately to keep v3 to the measured defect; it is the next cheap source, and it is already in the file c1 reads.
knownGaps.v1FormatRefused: a target still carrying the v1 object definition is refused, not annotated the old way. Legacy projects (mls-102046) therefore cannot be equipped without regenerating their page defs. cm2DefinitionKind already distinguishes the two shapes, so accepting both would be a small change if a legacy project ever needs it.
